chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
With regards to the found property, he should raise it (look for its owner) for a year, then it would be like the rest of his own wealth.

key_terms.يُعَرِّفُهَا: He should make it known / announce it

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling for found property (luqatah) and how long must one search for the owner?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the procedural timeline for 'luqatah' (found property), mandating a one-year period of public announcement to locate the owner. If the owner remains unidentified after this year, the finder acquires full ownership rights, treating the found item as their personal wealth. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic balance between preserving the rights of the original owner and preventing the stagnation of assets in the community.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Dawood Sirhan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘With regards to the found property, he should raise it (look for its owner) for a year, then it would be like the rest of his own wealth’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn abu Nasr from Dawud ibn Sarhan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
one who finds something of value must (continue to) announce his finding for one year. Thereafter it becomes like the rest of his property.” (Consult fatwa also)
